subject: Payment gateway throughput spike — VPC peering & proxy path investigation
messages:
From: PaymentsCo Ops <ops@paymentsco.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate / latency hitting Redwood API (payments path)

Aditya,

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency and 502/504 errors to Redwood's text generation endpoint used by our payment reconciliation flow around 14:50 PDT. Success rates dropped to ~60% and response times jumped from ~120ms to ~1.8s for the tokenized requests. This is impacting end-of-day reconciliation and causing batch retries to pile up.

We've attached a packet capture and a short latency summary. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (peering, proxies, NAT) or whether we should open a ticket with our cloud provider?

Quick facts:
- Environment: prod (paymentsco-account-prod)
- Region: us-west-2
- Impact: 3x latency, 40% error rate on /v1/generate (token-based)
- First observed: 2026-09-20T14:50:00Z

Attachments: paymentsco_trace_20260920.pcap, latency_summary_20sep.pdf, error_snapshot_502.png

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Sr. SRE, PaymentsCo
ops@paymentsco.com

-----
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency hitting Redwood API (payments path)

Thanks Samir — sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating internally and will get you an ETA in 30 minutes.

Vivek / Monica — looping you in for triage and customer comms. Initial asks:
- Can infra confirm any recent peering or NAT changes for our us-west-2 egress pools?
- Can the network team validate DNS resolution times for api.redwood.ai from PaymentsCo IPs and check for any proxy/firewall anomalies?
- If we need to route traffic to an alternate peering region, what is the expected cutover time?

Samir — we'll keep this thread for live updates.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: High error rate / latency hitting Redwood API (payments path)

Fwding PaymentsCo report. Initial triage notes below.

What we've done so far:
- Checked control plane: no deployments or routing policy changes in the last 48h.
- Observed elevated tail latencies from our us-west-2 egress pool starting 14:48 PDT; tokenization latency also increased for small seq lengths.
- Dataplane traces show a sudden rise in TCP retransmits on the path that correlates with PaymentsCo ASNs.

Hypothesis: asymmetric peering plus a transparent proxy in the customer's path (or their provider) is causing packet reordering and TCP stalls. DNS lookups appear normal but we're seeing intermittent NXDOMAIN responses cached by an upstream resolver for api.redwood.ai from two of their IP ranges.

Immediate plan (T0 + 60m):
- Rishi: run traceroutes and MTRs from our edge pods to listed PaymentsCo IPs; capture packet-level stats and share.
- Marissa: prepare a short customer-facing note; propose temporary routing via our us-east-1 peering (can be enabled per-customer) to avoid the affected backbone.
- Monica: coordinate with PaymentsCo for a parallel validation from their side (DNS TTLs, proxy logs).

Attachments: (internal) none — refer to customer's pcap.

Vivek
Director, Support Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: samir.patel@paymentsco.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency hitting Redwood API (payments path)

Team — here's a short status for the customer and for execs. Please treat as draft until we confirm routing test results.

Customer-facing summary (to send in 30m):
- We're aware of the elevated error rate and latency impacting your payment reconciliation jobs. Our engineering team is actively investigating root cause focused on network path anomalies between PaymentsCo and our us-west-2 egress.
- Next steps: live traceroutes and a temporary reroute test to our us-east-1 peering to confirm whether the issue is isolated to the us-west-2 path. We'll provide an update within 90 minutes.
- Impact mitigation: recommend stopping non-critical reconciliation retries for 30 minutes to avoid backpressure.

Exec note for internal leadership:
- Impact: PaymentsCo batch jobs failing — potential revenue reconciliation delays and SLA exposure.
- Risk: if errors persist, customer will request credits and may escalate to procurement.
- Ask: leadership visibility in case credits/contract exceptions are requested.

Planned customer attachment: latency_summary_20sep.pdf (redacted), suggested interim postmortem timeline.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 17:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate / latency hitting Redwood API (payments path)

Quick technical findings (from edge pods in us-west-2):
- Traceroute to PaymentsCo IP range shows asymmetric path: packets hop through a CDN vendor that reports queueing on hop 6-7 with 8-12% packet loss recorded during the incident window.
- MTR graphs attached (pasted below) show rising latency after hop 5 consistent with peering congestion.
- DNS: observed isolated NXDOMAIN responses from resolver x.x.x.x (PaymentsCo's primary) between 14:46-14:55 PDT; likely cached upstream causing intermittent name resolution failures.

Immediate suggestion: enable per-account reroute to us-east-1 peering for PaymentsCo while we coordinate with the CDN provider and PaymentsCo's networking team. Expected cutover time: ~8-12 minutes once the routing policy is applied and warmed.

Related links: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/paymentsco/overview (traces and MTRs appended)

- Rishi
SRE, Inference Platform

-----
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: samir.patel@paymentsco.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 18:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec: Payment gateway incident — action summary and next steps

Team / Samir,

Thank you for the fast collaboration. Short update for leadership and payment ops:
- What happened: transient path congestion and proxy-induced reordering on the egress path to PaymentsCo's ASN produced increased TCP retransmits, resulting in elevated latency and a spike in 502/504 responses between ~14:48-15:30 PDT.
- What we did: applied per-account reroute to us-east-1 peering (completed 17:12 PDT), verified success rates returned to baseline within ~6 minutes, collected packet captures and traceroutes, and engaged the CDN provider and PaymentsCo's network team for a joint investigation.
- Customer impact: temporary failures in reconciliation; PaymentsCo paused non-critical retries and resumed after reroute. They reported reduced error rates and normalized latency by 17:20 PDT.
- Next steps: joint postmortem with CDN provider + PaymentsCo, evaluate longer-term routing policy to avoid single-peering dependency, and review DNS resolver cache behavior with PaymentsCo.

If PaymentsCo requests credits, we should evaluate per our SLA (ops: please prepare an impact estimate and proposed credit).

Thanks all for the quick work — Monica please send the customer-facing summary and copy me.

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: latency_summary_20sep.pdf (sent to customer), paymentsco_trace_20260920.pcap (internal)
